claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch now based on aggregate readiness and rehearsal results, with documented monitoring, despite the unresolved debt-collection compliance gap and open disclosure question.
decision_criteria: Use 'compliant' only if admissible evidence shows the release policy threshold is satisfied, including any required disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
Execution-readiness evidence may support launch preparedness, but cannot by itself satisfy a separate disclosure predicate.
A weakness affecting a named launch use case is material under the provided policy unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Open legal review and unresolved materiality weigh against treating certification as fully supported.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the debt collection compliance gap must be disclosed before launch.
Evidence of approved risk acceptance covering this specific gap before launch, if disclosure will not be made.
Final launch documentation or model card showing the required disclosure, if that is the chosen control.
Authoritative evidence resolving whether the named servicing commitments make this a material named launch use case for release-policy purposes.
specific_concerns: Admissible evidence supports execution readiness, but not the unresolved policy predicate for launch disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
The debt collection compliance segment misses target and is a named launch use case via servicing rollout commitments, which makes the weakness potentially material under the stated policy.
The product's 'non-core' characterization does not resolve materiality under the policy text.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so the compliance basis for certifying now is unresolved.
Public model-card and AI-risk-management guidance support documentation and monitoring, but they do not substitute for satisfying the release policy's disclosure/acceptance requirement.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that current certification is clearly policy-compliant without a material weakness disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch.
Any claim that public governance guidance alone authorizes launch despite an unresolved materiality and disclosure question.
Any claim that the 'non-core' or low-volume characterization defeats materiality for a named committed segment.
